findings.title: text.blank? raises ArgumentError on malformed UTF-8 before text.scrub can clean it
findings.description: In both BulkChannelMessageSendJob#parse_text (line 52) and CreateStageAutomationMessage#parse_text (line 34), `text.blank?` is called before `text.scrub`. When text contains malformed UTF-8 bytes, String#blank? (ActiveSupport 6.1.7.7, Ruby 3.1.6) internally uses regex matching (/\A\s*\z/) which raises ArgumentError: 'invalid byte sequence in UTF-8'. The .scrub call on line 58/38 would fix the encoding, but it never executes because the exception is thrown first.

test_results.single_invalid_byte_0xFF: .blank? raised ArgumentError: invalid byte sequence in UTF-8; .scrub.blank? succeeded

findings.fix: Swap the order: call .scrub before .blank?, e.g., `return '' if text.scrub.blank?` then continue with the already-scrubbed string, or separate into `text = text.scrub; return '' if text.blank?`
findings.severity_rationale: Upgrading from LOW to MED. The bug is real and reproducible: any malformed UTF-8 in subject or body text will cause an unhandled ArgumentError. In practice, the controller layer sanitizes inputs via Sanitize.fragment (Nokogiri), which may normalize encoding for browser-submitted data. However, the automation path (HiringStageMessageAutomationJob) reads subject/body from stored ChannelMessageTemplate records, and the bulk message path processes text through Sidekiq job deserialization. Both paths could pass malformed UTF-8 if the database contains it. The exception is caught by the outer rescue StandardError in both files, so it doesn't crash the server, but it silently prevents message delivery with a generic error ('Message not sent. An unexpected error occurred') instead of sending the cleaned message. This is a silent functional failure, not just a theoretical concern.
findings.pre_existing_note: The .blank?-before-.scrub pattern exists in the original body-only code. The email-subjects feature copied this pattern for the subject field, propagating the bug. The bug affects both body and subject processing in both files.

findings.title: QA harness starts server from main checkout, not worktree
findings.description: The qa-config.yml declares source_repo as /Users/jessica/wrk/wrk-corp/inflow-ats (the main checkout). The ServerManager uses this as the cwd for subprocess.Popen (server.py line 239). When testing a worktree branch like inflow-ats.messaging-improvements, the server runs from the main checkout code, not the worktree code. This means the QA harness tests the main branch code, not the feature branch code.
findings.severity_rationale: Downgrading from LOW to INFO. This is a QA harness configuration issue, not a bug in the email-subjects feature code. The qa-config.yml is a shared config file that could be pointed at a worktree by passing a different config or overriding source_repo. It is a known limitation of the current qa-harness setup, not a finding against the feature under test. For this specific QA run, the script_runner layer uses test_frr directly from the worktree (cd to worktree + test_frr), so script_runner tests DO run against the feature branch code. Only the server-based layers (cypress, playwright_mcp) would be affected.
findings.pre_existing_note: This is a qa-harness infrastructure concern, not related to the email-subjects feature.

severity_changes.L2-001: LOW -> MED (validated as real bug, silent functional failure on malformed UTF-8)
severity_changes.L2-INFO-001: LOW -> INFO (validated but downgraded; qa-harness config concern, not feature bug)

summary.recommendation: L2-001 should be addressed: swap .scrub and .blank? ordering in both parse_text methods. The fix is a one-line change in each file. L2-INFO-001 is informational only and does not require action for this feature.
